+def _restore_acronyms(title: str, word: str) -> str:
+    """
+    Put the words of ``word`` that are written in capitals, such as acronyms,
+    back into ``title``, the titleized form of ``word``.
+
+    ``title`` holds the letters and digits of ``word`` in the same order, with
+    only their case changed (and a trailing ``"_id"`` dropped by
+    :func:`humanize`), so each of its words is matched with the same number
+    of letters and digits of ``word``.
+    """
+    original_characters = ''.join(re.findall(r"[^\W_]+", word))
+    # The words are at the odd indexes, with the text around them in between:
+    # 'Nasa Rocket' gives ['', 'Nasa', ' ', 'Rocket', ''].
+    pieces = re.split(r"([^\W_]+)", title)
+    position = 0
+    keep = False
+    for index in range(1, len(pieces), 2):
+        titled = pieces[index]
+        original = original_characters[position:position + len(titled)]
+        position += len(titled)
+        if (len(original) != len(titled) or
+                original.casefold() != titled.casefold()):
+            # A case change did not map one character to one (for example
+            # "ß" titleizes to "Ss"), so the words cannot be matched up.
+            return title
+        # titleize lowercases a letter after an apostrophe ("David's"), so a
+        # lone capital there is only kept as part of a word written in
+        # capitals ("DON'T").
+        after_apostrophe = index > 1 and pieces[index - 1] == "'"
+        keep = original.isupper() and (
+            len(original) > 1 or not after_apostrophe or keep
+        )
+        if keep:
+            pieces[index] = original
+    return ''.join(pieces)
+
+
